title: Towards a Simplified Numerical Methodology for Estimating the Efficiency of an Air Handling Unit
content: This work presents a study on the calculation of transmittance in an Air Handling Unit (AHU) through three methods: theoretical estimation, experimental approach and numerical simulations. First, a theoretical estimation based on simplified models of heat and mass transfer in the AHU was employed. In addition, experimental tests were carried out in a real AHU under controlled conditions, obtaining temperature measurements inside and outside the unit. These data were used to calculate the transmittance using predefined formulas. Finally, numerical simulations were performed on specific sections of the AHU and on a global model, with and without radiation considering its influence. The simulations provided detailed results on the flow behaviour and temperature distribution. The results obtained were compared and analysed to assess the accuracy and applicability of the three methods. This research contributes to the knowledge and understanding of transmittance in AHUs, providing valuable information for the design and optimisation of Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems.
